nodes.summary: Sets the core, bus and timer all to ICSOUTCLK; written after the ICS switch.

nodes.name: KE0x_OSC_InitHighGain
nodes.summary: Enables the crystal oscillator in high-gain, high-range mode and waits for it to initialize.

nodes.name: KE0x_ICS_SelectFllRefInternal
nodes.summary: Selects the slow internal reference clock as the FLL reference and waits for the switch.

nodes.name: KE0x_ICS_SelectFllRefExternal
nodes.summary: Selects the divided oscillator as the FLL reference with the given RDIV and waits for the switch.

nodes.name: KE0x_ICS_SelectOutFll
nodes.summary: Selects the FLL as ICSOUTCLK with the given BDIV output divider and waits for the clock status.

nodes.name: KE0x_ICS_WaitFllLock
nodes.summary: Waits for the FLL to lock, then clears the loss-of-lock flag.

nodes.name: KE0x_ICS_DisableIrclk
nodes.summary: Turns the internal reference clock output (ICSIRCLK) off in both run and stop modes.

nodes.name: _KE0x_InitClockExternal
nodes.summary: FLL-engaged-external boot sequence: dividers, oscillator, external FLL reference with the given RDIV, FLL output, lock wait.

nodes.name: KE0x_InitClockExternal
nodes.summary: Boot clock from the external crystal with RDIV 3, which on KE06 gives the crystal frequency times 5.

nodes.name: KE0x_InitClockInternal
nodes.summary: FLL-engaged-internal boot clock: core at the FLL output (48 MHz on KE06) and bus at half.

nodes.name: KE0x_InitClockReset
nodes.summary: Restores the reset-state clock (FEI, FLL / 2, core and bus at ICSOUTCLK, 24 MHz on KE06), keeping the bus at half until ICSOUTCLK has dropped.

nodes.name: svpwm_ceiling.py
nodes.summary: Python model of the firmware's svpwm_midclamp_ceiling zero-sequence placement (Motor/Motor/Math/svpwm_math.h): builds balanced three-phase voltages, computes the duties under a duty ceiling, classifies the clamp branch each vector takes, and derives the radii where the branch changes. Run as a script it prints per-radius duty statistics and renders SVPWM_Ceiling.png; it is also the base module the other SVPWM simulations import.

nodes.name: phase_voltages
nodes.summary: Returns a balanced three-phase voltage set of the given peak radius (per VBus) at angle theta, the input form the SVPWM clamp functions take.

nodes.name: math_clamp
nodes.summary: Clamps a value between a lower and an upper bound, mirroring the firmware's scalar clamp helper.

nodes.name: svpwm_midclamp_ceiling
nodes.summary: Simulates the firmware's svpwm_midclamp_ceiling: picks the zero-sequence voltage that puts the highest duty at the ceiling, held between midclamp's value and the bottom clamp's, and returns vZero, midclamp's vZero and the three phase duties.

nodes.name: simulate
nodes.summary: Runs svpwm_midclamp_ceiling over one electrical cycle at a given radius and returns a column array of vZero, midclamp vZero, the phase voltages and the duties.

nodes.name: regime_of
nodes.summary: Classifies each vector of a simulated cycle by the clamp branch it takes: midclamp, the ceiling, or the bottom clamp.

nodes.name: finish
nodes.summary: Applies the shared title, axis labels and grid styling to a matplotlib axis; every SVPWM figure script calls it.

nodes.name: svpwm_blend.py
nodes.summary: Python model of the firmware's general svpwm_clamp (Motor/Motor/Math/svpwm_math.h) fed a magnitude-keyed blend factor k that ramps from midclamp (k = 1/2) at VBus/2 down to the bottom clamp (k = 0) at the radius the low-side current-sense window allows. Run as a script it prints per-radius duty statistics and renders SVPWM_Blend_Magnitude.png; its constants and helpers are reused by the blend analysis and figure scripts.

nodes.name: blend_k
nodes.summary: Maps a magnitude to the clamp factor k: 1/2 up to the start value, falling linearly to 0 at the end value.

nodes.name: svpwm_clamp
nodes.summary: Simulates the firmware's svpwm_clamp: the general zero-sequence placement vZero = k*(vMax - 1) + (1 - k)*vMin, returning vZero and the three phase duties.

nodes.name: k_of_magnitude
nodes.summary: Computes the blend's k from the vector magnitude |v| = sqrt(2/3 * sum v^2), which is constant over an electrical cycle.

nodes.name: k_of_magnitude_squared
nodes.summary: Square-root-free variant of the blend's k, ramping linearly in |v|^2 against the squared ramp ends.

nodes.name: k_of_spread_ceiling
nodes.summary: Reference k of the per-vector duty-ceiling placement as a function of the spread vMax - vMin: (D - s)/(1 - s) held to [0, 1/2].

nodes.name: simulate
nodes.summary: Runs svpwm_clamp with a supplied k function over one electrical cycle at a radius and returns vZero, midclamp vZero, k, the phase voltages and the duties per sample.

nodes.name: regime_of
nodes.summary: Classifies each sample of a run as midclamp, ramp or bottom clamp from its k.

nodes.name: plot_text
nodes.summary: Converts formula text to its figure form by replacing 'sqrt3' with the square-root-of-3 glyph.

nodes.name: describe
nodes.summary: Builds a panel heading that names the radius and the k that holds over the whole cycle.

nodes.name: plot_cycles
nodes.summary: Renders six one-cycle panels of duties, phase voltages and vZero under the magnitude blend, each with a k color strip, and saves SVPWM_Blend_Magnitude.png.

nodes.name: svpwm_blend_analysis.py
nodes.summary: Sweeps the magnitude blend, its |v|^2 form and plain midclamp across vector magnitudes at import time, producing the per-radius duty, k and zero-sequence shift extrema that the blend figure scripts plot. Run as a script it prints the inflection radii, consistency checks and a low-side window table.
nodes.languageNotes: The sweeps run at module level, so importing the module executes them and exposes the resulting NumPy arrays as module attributes for the figure scripts.

nodes.name: mark_inflections
nodes.summary: Draws vertical markers, optionally labeled, at the radii where the blend ramp starts and ends.

nodes.name: sweep
nodes.summary: For each radius in the grid, simulates one cycle with a given k function and collects the min and max of the highest, middle and lowest duties, of k, and of the vZero shift from midclamp.

nodes.name: svpwm_blend_duty.py
nodes.summary: Figure script plotting each duty's range over a cycle against vector magnitude under the magnitude blend, with midclamp's peaks and today's low-side window for reference; saves SVPWM_Blend_Duty.png.

nodes.name: svpwm_blend_k.py
nodes.summary: Figure script comparing k over a cycle against vector magnitude: the magnitude blend's single k and its |v|^2 form against the duty-ceiling placement's per-vector range; saves SVPWM_Blend_K.png.

nodes.name: svpwm_blend_schedule.py
nodes.summary: Figure script plotting k, the top phase's low-side window and the lowest phase's on time against the spread vMax - vMin for midclamp, the duty ceiling and the bottom clamp, with the magnitude blend overlaid as one segment per radius; saves SVPWM_Blend_Schedule.png.

nodes.name: svpwm_blend_shift.py
nodes.summary: Figure script showing how far the magnitude blend lowers the zero-sequence voltage below midclamp's across one 60 degree sector for several radii; saves SVPWM_Blend_Shift.png.

nodes.name: svpwm_ceiling_analysis.py
nodes.summary: Sweeps svpwm_midclamp_ceiling and plain midclamp across vector magnitudes at import time, producing the per-radius duty and spread extrema and the exact share of the cycle on each clamp branch for the ceiling figure scripts. Run as a script it prints the inflection radii, consistency checks and a duty comparison table.
nodes.languageNotes: The sweeps run at module level, so importing the module executes them and exposes the resulting NumPy arrays as module attributes for the figure scripts.

nodes.name: share_beyond
nodes.summary: Computes analytically the share of an electrical cycle whose spread exceeds a threshold at a given radius.

nodes.name: mark_inflections
nodes.summary: Draws vertical markers, optionally labeled, at the radii where the ceiling's clamp branch changes.

nodes.name: sweep
nodes.summary: For each radius in the grid, simulates one cycle at a duty ceiling and collects the duty and spread extrema plus the sampled share of each clamp branch.

nodes.name: svpwm_ceiling_compare.py
nodes.summary: Figure script comparing the peak highest and middle duties over a cycle for svpwm_midclamp against svpwm_midclamp_ceiling across vector magnitudes; saves SVPWM_Ceiling_Compare.png.

nodes.name: svpwm_ceiling_duty.py
nodes.summary: Figure script plotting the range of the highest and lowest duties over a cycle under svpwm_midclamp_ceiling against vector magnitude; saves SVPWM_Ceiling_Duty.png.

nodes.name: svpwm_ceiling_regime.py
nodes.summary: Figure script drawing a stacked plot of the share of the cycle spent on the midclamp, ceiling and bottom-clamp branches against vector magnitude; saves SVPWM_Ceiling_Regime.png.

nodes.name: svpwm_ceiling_spread.py
nodes.summary: Figure script explaining where the branch inflections fall: the band of the spread vMax - vMin over a cycle crossing the thresholds 2D - 1 and D; saves SVPWM_Ceiling_Spread.png.

nodes.name: isample_model.py
nodes.summary: Timing model of the current-loop sample sequence on a KE06-class MCU: the PWM period and its load points, ADC conversion timing, estimated ISR segment durations, the Seq description of one sequencing variant, and Sim, a two-level preemptive scheduler that plays the PWM and ADC ISRs. Also provides the search helpers for the latest trigger start and for the duration-factor range over which a sequence keeps its load point.
nodes.languageNotes: Each ISR body is a Python generator yielding timed segments; the scheduler resumes whichever generator holds priority, which models interrupt preemption without threads.

nodes.name: walk_conv
nodes.summary: Returns the conversion time of an n-channel ADC FIFO: 2.5 us for the first channel and 2 us for each later one.

nodes.name: Seq
nodes.summary: Describes one current-loop sequencing variant: the ADC ISR priority, where the Park and the PI run, software or hardware trigger and its lead, VBus handling, request placement, the control-cycle divider and what the PWM ISR between control cycles does.

nodes.name: Sim
nodes.summary: Discrete-time simulation of one sequence: schedules PWM and ADC ISR releases, runs them as generator-defined segments under NVIC-style priority preemption, records the execution trace, ADC batches and duty writes, and reports the sample-to-load results.

nodes.name: Sim.loop_take
nodes.summary: Generator for the control loop's take of a captured current set: optionally spins until the capture arrives, then Parks and runs the PI.

nodes.name: Sim.pwm_isr
nodes.summary: Generator yielding the PWM ISR's segments for one tick: the ADC start or the mark-and-arm, sensor angle, state machine, requests, SetTheta, the loop's take and the duty write, in the order the sequence's options select.

nodes.name: Sim.adc_isr
nodes.summary: Generator yielding the ADC completion ISR's segments: the VBus and current capture, an optional Park, and an optional PI and duty write at the completion.

nodes.name: Sim.run
nodes.summary: Advances time in 0.05 us steps, firing due events, picking the job to run by priority and IRQ number, and extending the execution trace until the end time.

nodes.name: Sim.result
nodes.summary: Summarizes one batch: the sample time, the Park angle tick and its offset, PI end, write and load times, the sample-to-load delay, CPU busy time per period, arm margins and the PWM ISR start delay.

nodes.name: variant
nodes.summary: Returns a shallow copy of a sequence with the given attributes changed.

nodes.name: at_start
nodes.summary: Runs a sequence with its set started a given lead before the counter top and returns tick 0's result.

nodes.name: latest_lead
nodes.summary: Scans leads in 1 us and then 0.1 us steps for the latest trigger start whose taking cycle still takes its set and writes in time for the given load point.

nodes.name: k_range
nodes.summary: Finds the range of the duration factor k, within 0.5 to 1.5, over which a sequence keeps its nominal load point and its take still finds the set.

nodes.name: delay_clock
nodes.summary: Returns the smallest bus-clock divider whose 8-bit trigger delay, counted from the counter bottom, reaches the given start.

nodes.name: start_text
nodes.summary: Formats a lead as 'N us before the top' or 'after the top' for tables and figure labels.

nodes.name: isample_plots.py
nodes.summary: Matplotlib figure builders for the current-loop sequence simulation: one timeline per sequence, several sequences compared on a shared time axis, the trigger start calibration, and the sweep summary over the duration factor k.

nodes.name: conv_color
nodes.summary: Returns the bar color of an ADC conversion, distinguishing VSOURCE from the phase current channels.

nodes.name: cycle_label
nodes.summary: Labels the PWM cycle at tick n as the one that starts or takes the set, the off cycle, or the between cycle that marks and arms.

nodes.name: _counter
nodes.summary: Draws the center-aligned FTM2 counter triangle with a marker at each top and bottom load point.

nodes.name: _conversions
nodes.summary: Draws each ADC batch's conversions and any extra-channel walks as bars on the ADC lane.

nodes.name: _trace
nodes.summary: Draws the simulation's ISR execution segments as colored bars on the ADC ISR and PWM ISR lanes.

nodes.name: _legend
nodes.summary: Adds the figure legend that maps segment colors to their kinds.

nodes.name: plot_sequence
nodes.summary: Renders one sequence's timeline: the counter, ADC conversions, ISR lanes, the sample-to-load arrow, the Park angle marker and a note box, and saves it to a PNG.

nodes.name: plot_order_compare
nodes.summary: Runs and renders several sequences as stacked panels on one time axis around the taking cycle's top, marking each write and its load point.

nodes.name: plot_start_calibration
nodes.summary: Plots, against the set's start time, the wait the take would need and the sample-to-load delay for each variant at several k, with the bus-clock delay reach shaded.

nodes.name: plot_summary
nodes.summary: Plots the sample-to-load delay, the CPU time in the sampling cycle and the Park angle offset against the duration factor k for every sequence.

nodes.name: isample_sequences.py
nodes.summary: Catalog of the current-loop sequencing variants the built form was chosen from (software start, PI at the completion, and the triggered before, after, +V, bottom and every forms), held as Seq objects with trigger leads calibrated by simulation at import time, generated notes, and the comparison row tables the runner prints and plots.
nodes.languageNotes: Trigger leads, reference results and notes are computed by running simulations at module level, so importing the module executes the model.

nodes.name: by
nodes.summary: Looks up a sequence in SEQS by its key.

nodes.name: pwm_sample_sequences.py
nodes.summary: Runner script for the current-loop sequence study: simulates every sequence, prints the nominal, k-sweep, loop-order and triggered-by-load-point tables to the console and to pwm_sample_sequences.txt, and writes the timeline, panel, start-calibration and summary figures beside the file.

nodes.name: Tee
nodes.summary: File-like object that duplicates everything written to stdout into a text file.

nodes.name: ARCHITECTURE.md
nodes.summary: Top-level architecture reference for the library: the motor control feature set, the design patterns (compile-time HAL, const descriptors, hierarchical state machine, fixed-point quantities, pure math layer, decoupled protocols), Mermaid layer and motor-stack dependency diagrams, integration steps with the thread entry-point table, and an annotated directory map.
nodes.languageNotes: The Mermaid flowcharts encode the layering rule: arrows point from a module to what it depends on, and nothing includes upward.

nodes.name: CLAUDE.md
nodes.summary: Agent and contributor guidance for the library: core principles, documentation rules, the task workflow, the toolchain (C23, arm-none-eabi-gcc, no in-repo build), and the coding conventions for architecture patterns, naming, API design and API scoping.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Project landing page: introduces the embedded C motor control library, its highlights and FOC features, the layer layout (Motor, Peripheral, System, Transducer, Math, Framework), and links to the deeper module notes and the GPL-3.0 license.

nodes.name: library.json
nodes.summary: Dormant PlatformIO library manifest, commented out in full: package metadata and a source filter that selected the serial protocol sources for an Arduino-compatible commander build. Most of the listed source paths no longer exist, and the library builds inside the consuming board project instead.
nodes.languageNotes: Every line is a `//` comment, so the file is not valid JSON and no tool consumes it.

nodes.name: ApiScoping.md
nodes.summary: Rules for scoping function parameters and names: a function takes the narrowest struct it reads or writes, its scope prefix follows the widest struct its effects reach, and a leading underscore marks module-internal helpers. Applies the interface segregation principle.

nodes.name: Comments.md
nodes.summary: Commenting convention: a comment holds only the rationale the code cannot state, and facts move into names, literals and static_assert. Adds a layout rule that sets parallel clauses as aligned rows, shown on the svpwm_clamp comment.

nodes.name: ConditionalCompilation.md
nodes.summary: Convention for sparing use of preprocessor paths: variants are named functions compiled in every build, one #if selection point dispatches to them, optional runtime modes select through a predicate, and guards go around references rather than definitions.

nodes.name: ConfigValidity.md
nodes.summary: Convention that validity is a config invariant checked once at the config layer: conversions and derivations carry no guards, each sub-struct has its own IsValid composed by the outer check, and Validate repairs where IsValid faults.

nodes.name: Config_State_Ref.md
nodes.summary: Convention separating persisted Config_T data from runtime state so each persisted value has one writable copy. Gives two options, flat non-nesting config partitions held by the runtime or a runtime that holds only a derived Ref, plus mirror fields and the id-keyed config interface.

nodes.name: FixedPoint.md
nodes.summary: Reference for the fixed-point quantity system: stored values belong to a per-unit, time (ticks of a named clock) or angle (turn / 2^16) family, each with its bases, types, arithmetic forms and the bridge constants between families. Closes with 13 rules, a viability assessment with measured ranges, one finding and open questions.

nodes.name: HardwareBinding.md
nodes.summary: Ten rules for code that binds a peripheral to the application (HAL functions, board setup, binding header), drawn from the ADC scan on an S32K1 board with PDB and eDMA. Each rule names what it replaces, such as per-variant resource sets, register read-back and config structs feeding long init signatures.

nodes.name: InitMacros.md
nodes.summary: Convention for when an *_INIT macro earns its place over designated initializers: it casts a handler, sizes flexible-array state, derives a field, or builds a constant expression. RING_T_INIT_AS in RingT.h is the reference case.

nodes.name: MergingDuplicates.md
nodes.summary: Convention for merging near-duplicate functions into one generic only when every caller passes real arguments, with the accepted s/rad conversion pair and the rejected pu_tau_of_angle_freq merge, which needed a placeholder base, as examples.

nodes.name: ModeOverBool.md
nodes.summary: Convention that a gate, enable or pause on a state struct is a value of an enum mode the poll switches on, not a single-purpose bool. Existing enums are extended first, and DISABLED = 0 keeps a zero-initialized struct safe.

nodes.name: Naming.md
nodes.summary: Naming convention for the library: underscores separate scope segments and case separates words, with rules for types, variables, functions, the verb vocabulary, unit suffixes, word order and build-option macros. The tail holds unfinished notes on type-role suffixes and module directory layout.

nodes.name: ValueOverBool.md
nodes.summary: Convention that an on/off already decided by a value parameter is that value's degenerate case (a limit or gain of 0) rather than a bool beside it, worked through the field-weakening Id limit. States the cost: disabling discards the tuned value.

nodes.name: 0001_ParameterWriteAdmission.md
nodes.summary: Decision record (accepted): write admission for parameters that are unsafe to change while running belongs to the controller layer. The motor module keeps its schema, its setters and the state machine that gates the phase outputs.

nodes.name: 0002_LinearThrottleLayering.md
nodes.summary: Decision record (accepted, not yet implemented): Traction interprets a single-axis throttle lever and emits a signed calibrated-frame command, while Motor owns continuity through zero speed and the anti-plugging voltage limit.

nodes.name: 0003_PhaseOutputOwnership.md
nodes.summary: Decision record (accepted for now): every state loop that produces FOC output writes duty through Motor_FOC_WriteDuty right after its producer and the PWM thread writes none, so hold states keep the V0 safety short. Lists the deferred duty-domain output image and its open questions.

nodes.name: 0004_PiSlidingAntiWindup.md
nodes.summary: Decision record (accepted after a hardware test): the PI integral clamp uses the sliding band [OutputMin - P, OutputMax - P] clipped to the output range. The anchored form limit-cycled against the field-weakening loop and stays commented out.

nodes.name: 0005_ILimitFrames.md
nodes.summary: Decision record (accepted): current-limit derates split per quadrant, and each limit is keyed by the frame it is defined in: supply by the sign of v_q, motoring/generating by Direction, forward/reverse by absolute torque direction. The resolved window is their intersection.

nodes.name: 0006_RampLimitsOnInput.md
nodes.summary: Decision record (accepted): ramp limits clamp the ramp input each step rather than its output, so an output outside new bounds returns at the ramp slope. A protective limit drop therefore reaches the current loop at that slope.

nodes.name: 0007_SpeedPuBound.md
nodes.summary: Decision record (accepted): per-unit speed never exceeds 1.0, the bound of the speed PID input, so field weakening runs inside the same speed loop and Speed_Pu saturation is the intended bound.

nodes.name: 0008_PersistenceById.md
nodes.summary: Decision record (accepted): tools and the app address persisted config values by id through the VarId / ConfigId interface, never by struct offset. Persisted struct layouts may change freely; the id tables are the stable interface.

nodes.name: 0009_DirectionPolicy.md
nodes.summary: Decision record (proposed, deferred): replaces the Direction lock's anti-plugging half-plane with a voltage window around back EMF, clamped into the voltage circle, where the setter called is the policy. Lists the readers that must change first and the helper functions added but not yet wired.

nodes.name: 0010_SharedWordWrites.md
nodes.summary: Decision record (proposed, open): three values cross threads as multi-word or read-modify-write stores (ISupplyLimits, the PID gains, FaultFlags) and can be read torn. Lists four options, from writer critical sections to single-writer ownership, with none chosen.

nodes.name: 0011_StateMachineLockNesting.md
nodes.summary: Decision record (proposed, open): the state-machine async lock enables interrupts unconditionally on release, so a handler that sends an input to another machine unlocks the rest of the outer handler. Lists four options, undecided, to be settled together with 0010.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Index and format guide for the architecture decision records, following Nygard's ADR shape (Status, Context, Decision, Consequences). Holds a status table of records 0001 to 0009 and names one pending decision.

nodes.name: 2026-10-14_CorruptLooseBlobs.md
nodes.summary: Dated finding on why `git log -S` errors on the library repo: three corrupt loose blobs holding old versions of three source files, with a move-aside and refetch fix that was not yet applied as of 2026-10-29.

nodes.name: 2026-11-04_HwScanBindingSimplification.md
nodes.summary: Dated finding comparing a board binding for a hardware-sequenced ADC scan at 2026-09-25 and 2026-11-04: one completion ISR instead of two and no branches in it, attributed to seven of the ten HardwareBinding rules, with the costs and what was not measured.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Index of the Findings folder: defines a finding as a dated measurement or source read that backs the Decisions, gives the Question / Method / Result / Conclusion entry shape, and lists the recorded findings.

nodes.name: Descriptor.md
nodes.summary: Architectural pattern sheet for the const descriptor: a `typedef const struct` holding bindings, compile-time constants and pointers to mutable parts, which the compiler folds at inlined call sites as C's stand-in for a template argument. Covers the module and template forms, measured folding behaviour on Cortex-M0+, code instances and rejected alternatives.

nodes.name: DescriptorPattern.md
nodes.summary: Architectural pattern sheet for hardware-bound modules: one aggregate root per storage region, with the `Module_T` descriptor in FLASH, `Module_State_T` in RAM and `Module_Config_T` in NVM, all reached through a single handle. Uses `Hall_T` as the worked example and cites Zephyr's device model as precedent.

nodes.name: DescriptorTemplate.md
nodes.summary: Idiom sheet for generic primitives specialized by a descriptor: the shape (element size and length, time source and frequency) is a const argument passed beside the state, so one body compiles to a hard-coded copy per shape, as in `RingT` and `TimerT`. Defines the pure, primitive and handle layers, a proposed by-value or by-reference passing rule, and open inconsistencies between Ring and Timer.

nodes.name: EdgePollSnapshot.md
nodes.summary: Idiom sheet for edge detectors that wrap a poll writing the value they compare: snapshot the prior value into a local first, because the operands of `!=` are unsequenced in C and the one-line form is undefined behaviour. Lists the three detectors fixed this way.

nodes.name: EnumNamedValues.md
nodes.summary: Idiom sheet for enums whose enumerators are values of the quantity they classify, either range lower bounds or signed levels, so classification is a mask, sign, `abs` or product instead of a table or switch. States the rules (closed set, zero is neutral, cast once, values are the contract), the code instances and the MISRA deviations it costs.

nodes.name: EquationStruct.md
nodes.summary: Design pattern sheet for stateful math modules: each struct is one published equation with its coefficients and state bound as fields, inputs passed as arguments and shared outputs stored. Defines the coefficient, state, input and output roles, how coefficients map to a structured state-space form, and why indexed coefficient matrices and per-physical-part types were rejected.

nodes.name: Facets.md
nodes.summary: Architectural pattern sheet for objects that serve several kinds of client: one header per concern (user commands, variable system, control math, state machine), each a complete view of the same shared state. Applied to `Motor_T` and `MotorController_T`, with faceted classification and role interfaces as sources.

nodes.name: FunctionPointerCasting.md
nodes.summary: Draft notes, not yet in the pattern entry shape, on typing protocol request handlers with their real context and payload types and casting once at the `PROTOCOL_REQ` table row. Explains what a handler may narrow, when to keep `void *`, and why the cast is formally undefined yet safe under AAPCS.
nodes.languageNotes: Calling through a function pointer cast from a signature with narrowed object-pointer parameters is undefined in ISO C; it holds here because every object pointer passes as one register word under AAPCS.

nodes.name: GuardedCall.md
nodes.summary: Idiom sheet for optional features: compile the definitions in every build, put the `#if` around the single reference (call, table row or entry body), and let `--gc-sections` drop the unreferenced code at link. Records the measured link results and the limit that a compiled definition can still change inlining in its translation unit.

nodes.name: HwSequencedScan.md
nodes.summary: Design pattern sheet for hardware-triggered ADC scans copied by DMA: channel sets are const `ADC_Sequence_T` records, the active and next set live in an `ADC_SequenceTrigger_T` owned by the library, and one completion ISR applies the switch and runs the set's map. Includes the board binding sketch, limits and the rejected per-set and per-mode alternatives.

nodes.name: ProtocolStack.md
nodes.summary: Architectural pattern sheet for wire protocols: a generic engine driven by an opaque-context callback table, a small device integration exposing explicit-pair functions, typed-union payloads and compile-time spec metadata. Lists nine rules with the CiA 402 stack as the reference shape for new protocols.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Index of the pattern catalogue: defines the architectural, design and idiom levels, the required entry shape (Level, Force, Shape, In code, Rejected, Source), and a table of the eleven written patterns with when to apply each, plus one candidate not yet written up.

nodes.name: WrapperSurface.md
nodes.summary: Design pattern sheet for how an outer module exposes an inner one or couples two peers: each operation is a forwarder, a getter or an adaptation, chosen by tests on state ownership and API size. Also sets when peers need free-function bridges, a mediator or a facade, and when a wrapper type earns its existence.

nodes.name: DominantDecomposition.md
nodes.summary: Principle that a folder tree or type hierarchy carries only one axis of a classification, so the structural axis is chosen on purpose and every other axis gets a named mechanism; sourced from the tyranny of the dominant decomposition and faceted classification.

nodes.name: InformationExpert.md
nodes.summary: Principle (GRASP Information Expert) that each layer answers only the questions it alone has the knowledge for; parameter write admission is the worked example, splitting motor-domain checks from the controller's lifecycle checks.

nodes.name: InterfaceSegregation.md
nodes.summary: Principle that a function signature is a capability contract: interfaces expose the minimum a client needs and functions take the narrowest struct holding what they read or write, which also lowers physical header dependencies.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Index of the Principles folder: defines a principle as the reason behind conventions, patterns and decisions, gives the TOGAF-style Statement / Rationale / Implications / Source entry shape, and lists the four written principles.

nodes.name: StructSemantics.md
nodes.summary: Principle that a struct's kind (who writes it, when, where it lives and how it is passed) decides its storage, passing form and API, not its shape. Tabulates eight kinds, from compile-time context and HAL descriptor to value, data model and packet, with exemplar types and the AAPCS limits on passing by value.

nodes.name: Architecture.md
nodes.summary: Architecture reference for the hierarchical state machine engine: const State_T nodes in ROM form a parent-pointer tree with one active-leaf pointer in RAM per instance. Covers the layers and files, handler semantics, the tree walk with entry/exit, one proc cycle, inputs, threads and the lock, path ids, and the motor instance as wired.

nodes.name: InputVsLoop.md
nodes.summary: Traces where the periodic LOOP and the asynchronous inputs of the Motor and MotorController machine instances meet the shared active-state pointer under STATE_MACHINE_ASYNC_CRITICAL. Shows the half-made transition window, the unlocked main-thread transitions and the nested lock release that open decisions 0010 and 0011 are about; proposes no fix.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Index for the StateMachine module: states the model in one line and links the architecture sheet, the public API and node definition headers, the flat and hierarchical engine sources, the thread compositions and the two open thread decisions.

nodes.name: DependencyGraph.md
nodes.summary: Include graph of the `Motor/Motor` and `Motor/MotorController` headers as two Mermaid flowcharts: arrows run from each header to the headers it includes, and edges implied by a longer path are left out.

nodes.name: StateMachineOverview.md
nodes.summary: Overview and design record of the two hierarchical state machines of motor control: the per-motor `MSM_MACHINE` on the PWM thread and the controller's `MCSM_MACHINE` on the main thread, with app sub-states such as Traction mounted under `MC_STATE_MAIN`. Covers layer ownership, cross-layer interlocks, the engine conventions both rely on, the design decisions and the open items.

nodes.name: ThreadOwnership.md
nodes.summary: Reference sheet of every `Motor_Context_T`, `FOC_T` and `MotorController_Context_T` field that one execution context writes and another reads (PWM ISR, ADC ISR, 1 ms timer ISR, locked and unlocked main loop): writer, reader, width and whether the store is a single word. Locates the multi-word crossings recorded in Decisions 0010 and 0011 without proposing locks.

nodes.name: ControlCycleDataFlow.md
nodes.summary: Follows one current-loop control cycle from ADC counts to the PWM compare registers, one lane per thread. Names the FOC_T / Motor_Context_T field, fixed-point unit and owning thread for each step: sample, per-unit conversion, Clarke/Park, the d and q PI, inverse transforms, SVPWM zero sequence and the duty write.

nodes.name: LimitChain.md
nodes.summary: One-picture map of the motor limit chain: the V side (modulation circle, d band, q budget, VLimit half-plane, field weakening) and the I side (motoring/generating limits, supply window, torque ramp) meeting at the current PI. Tabulates where and how often each node is re-evaluated and the preset macros that select its variant.

nodes.name: Motor_StateMachine.md
nodes.summary: Module sheet for the per-motor state machine (MSM_MACHINE): the threads it runs on, the root states and their transitions, inputs and the interface functions that send them, direction handling, fault flags, the INTERVENTION supervisor, and the OPEN_LOOP and CALIBRATION sub-states.

nodes.name: Motor_StateTree.md
nodes.summary: Full state tree of one motor's machine, roots and leaves, with every hand-off. Includes how the engine's walk is used, per-branch state diagrams, a responsibility matrix (ENTRY output and timers, LOOP, duty write, NEXT targets, actions, mapped inputs) and the entry points for the sensorless, encoder, open-loop, intervention and calibration leaves.

nodes.name: LimitPhysics.md
nodes.summary: Explains which current or voltage bound binds where and why each limit frame needs its key: the supply (DC) limit mapped to i_q by power balance or phase bound, rollback under the VLimit half-plane, standstill and stall behaviour, ramp and speed lead, operating-point checks, and bus voltage and energy margins, with worked numbers.

nodes.name: ModulationLimit.md
nodes.summary: Describes how the low-side current-sense window sets the current loop's modulation limit (FOC_V_CIRCLE_PER_V_BUS), the SVPWM zero-sequence placement options (midclamp, midclamp ceiling, fixed clamp) and their ripple cost, and the svpwm_math.h macros that give the largest circle radius for a sensing window.

nodes.name: VLimitPolicy.md
nodes.summary: Design note on the q-axis voltage band of the current loop (FOC_T VLimit): how the circle, static shape, dynamic side and window compose, how a v_q band maps to a reachable i_q band, and how each policy behaves in braking, hill hold and through zero speed. The band is designed but not wired; the wiring steps and the PI structure are listed.

nodes.name: motor_electrical_math.md
nodes.summary: Reference for the per-unit speed bases of the motor electrical model: the turn base versus the speed base, the flux and inductance per-unit conversions and their rounding, inductance stored as a rate, storage in Motor_Electrical_T versus the derived FOC and observer views, the Kv convention, and worked numeric examples.

nodes.name: Sensorless.exp.md
nodes.summary: Detail companion to Sensorless.md: why the observer predicts and corrects as it does, the EEMF sliding-mode front end and the PLL tracker, state layout, the start-up failure and its fix, float-plant results per front end, the wiring history, options evaluated but not built, and the open list.

nodes.name: Sensorless.md
nodes.summary: Module sheet for sensorless rotor angle estimation: the extended-EMF sliding-mode observer behind the RotorSensor interface and its start-up chain. Covers the structure and layering, one control cycle's predict/correct sequence, the correction's constraints, signal flow, the timeline on the current-loop sequence, init and selection, and the sensorless states.

nodes.name: SensorlessMath.md
nodes.summary: Presents the math under EmfObserver_T and AnglePll_T as geometry: the stator voltage polygon, Clarke/Park frames and the hold angle, the SMO switch with its balance point and orbit, the low-pass filter, the quarter-turn detector and the PLL, each tied to its C function and to figures from the simulation scripts.

nodes.name: ADC_Batch_JoinVariants.md
nodes.summary: Working note on an open ADC_Batch decision: whether the join must reprogram every part or each ADC may start its own next sequence at its completion. Records the measured variants A to E from the batch test, the three rules variant C needs, its one cost, what it buys, and the proposal if taken.

nodes.name: Notes.md
nodes.summary: Design reference for coordinating an ADC conversion set spread over several converters: the five jobs (start, sequence, transfer, join, select), trigger-owned versus converter-owned sets, how generic frameworks such as Linux IIO define them, how a set learns every converter is done, how this module applies it, open design points and the S32K1 board's sequence-only case.

nodes.name: VariantMap.md
nodes.summary: Map of the ADC module's activation styles (pull, hardware-triggered FIFO, hardware-sequenced DMA, software walk, software sequence, batch, polled completion), which board preset builds each, the shared state words each touches, and which styles are live, test-only or dead.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: States the placement rule for module notes: they live beside the source they describe, with stack-wide notes at the stack root, instead of being mirrored under Docs/Modules. Cross-module rules go to Conventions and Patterns, and the sheet/detail pair is Topic.md plus Topic.exp.md.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Index of the Docs folder: a table of Principles, Conventions, Patterns, Decisions, Findings and Modules with what each holds and its entry format, followed by the placement rules for the library's own notes, module notes and drafts.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Housekeeping note: the folder still holds three reference PDFs (MCUBOOTRM, n1169, n3574) that are to move to the Ref folder, after which this folder can be removed.

nodes.name: Datagram.md
nodes.summary: Module note for the Datagram var-streaming mode over the Protocol request engine: a CONFIG_ID frame installs a var-id and width mapping whole or not at all, DATA_ID frames carry raw packed values, and the host paces the stream by acks until the cycle budget, an abort frame or a request timeout ends the run.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Protocol engine overview: Mermaid diagrams of the receive pipeline (Rx parser, classify, sync, request, compose, transport) and the packet Rx parser states, followed by flow traces for the four request shapes the request table uses: stateless, stateless with ack, ack-paced stream and data-paced sink.

nodes.name: comments.md
nodes.summary: Explains the two selectable Protocol consistency checks, PROTOCOL_CHECK_RX_FRAME_CONSISTENCY and PROTOCOL_CHECK_TX_FRAME_BOUNDS: what each one guards against and the codec and request-table conditions under which it is dead code or a live runtime guard.

nodes.name: Ring.c
nodes.summary: Legacy implementation of the generic ring buffer (push and pop at both ends, enqueue and dequeue of N units, peek, optional local critical section), kept fully commented out beside the active RingT headers. Compiles to nothing.

nodes.name: Ring.h
nodes.summary: Legacy ring buffer header, fully commented out: index-mode selection (power-of-two counter, power-of-two wrap, length compare), full and empty count helpers and the Ring_* API declarations. Superseded by the RingT headers.

nodes.name: StateMachine_Part.h
nodes.summary: Draft StateMachine extension header whose only live content is its includes. The commented-out sketch splits the machine into a part-state struct and a sync-input struct with a bit-mask loop that dispatches each pending input.

nodes.name: _StateMachine_FaultState.c
nodes.summary: Generic fault-state template for the StateMachine: resolves the machine's fault state and fault input id, stores the fault flags, and exposes set, clear, enter and exit fault calls that post an async transition input carrying set and clear flag deltas.
nodes.languageNotes: Fault-state access compiles to a stub unless STATE_MACHINE_FAULT_STATE_ENABLE is defined. Set and clear deltas are packed into one input value through a union compound literal.

nodes.name: FaultState
nodes.summary: Returns the machine's designated fault state, or NULL when the fault-state option is compiled out.

nodes.name: FaultState_SetFlags
nodes.summary: Overwrites the active state machine's fault flags when the fault-state option is enabled.

nodes.name: FaultState_GetFlags
nodes.summary: Reads the active fault flags, returning 0 when the fault-state option is compiled out.

nodes.name: FaultState_FaultId
nodes.summary: Returns the input id used for fault commands: STATE_MACHINE_FAULT_INPUT_ID when defined, otherwise the last entry of the transition table.

nodes.name: StateMachine_IsFault
nodes.summary: Tests whether the machine's active state is its fault state.

nodes.name: StateMachine_SetFault
nodes.summary: Posts an async tree transition input on the fault id carrying the flags to set, so the fault handler ORs them in atomically.

nodes.name: StateMachine_ClearFault
nodes.summary: Posts an async tree transition input on the fault id carrying the flags to clear.

nodes.name: StateMachine_ExitFault
nodes.summary: Clears all fault flags and reports whether the machine has left the fault state.

nodes.name: StateMachine_EnterFault
nodes.summary: Re-posts the stored fault flags as a set-fault input to drive the machine into the fault state.

nodes.name: _StateMachine_Linked.c
nodes.summary: Fully commented-out draft of a linked-menu StateMachine extension: a next-menu link per state with set-menu, start-menu and next-menu calls built on the base input and transition functions. Compiles to nothing.

nodes.name: Transient.c
nodes.summary: Implements the one-shot transient recorder: arm, disarm, start and stop control, trigger polling with edge or level comparison against a threshold, and per-call sampling of a 1, 2 or 4 byte variable into the caller's buffer until it fills.

nodes.name: ReadSized
nodes.summary: Reads a 1, 2 or 4 byte signed value through a volatile pointer and widens it to int32.

nodes.name: WriteSized
nodes.summary: Stores an int32 value into a 1, 2 or 4 byte destination slot.

nodes.name: TriggerFires
nodes.summary: Evaluates the trigger condition for the configured mode: level high or low, or a rising or falling edge using the previous sample. Manual mode never fires.

nodes.name: Transient_Init
nodes.summary: Resets the recorder state to idle with a manual trigger and zeroes the sample buffer.

nodes.name: Transient_Configure
nodes.summary: Sets the trigger type and threshold and discards the previous trigger sample.

nodes.name: Transient_Reset
nodes.summary: Returns the recorder to idle and clears the sample index, missed count and trigger tick.

nodes.name: Transient_Arm
nodes.summary: Resets the recorder and arms it so trigger polling becomes active.

nodes.name: Transient_Disarm
nodes.summary: Returns an armed recorder to idle without touching a recording in progress.

nodes.name: Transient_Start
nodes.summary: Starts recording from sample 0 immediately, bypassing the trigger.

nodes.name: Transient_Stop
nodes.summary: Ends a recording in progress early by marking it complete.

nodes.name: Transient_PollTrigger
nodes.summary: While armed, reads the trigger variable, evaluates the trigger condition and switches to recording when it fires.

nodes.name: Transient_Sample
nodes.summary: While recording, copies one sample of the recorded variable into the buffer and marks the capture complete when the buffer is full.

nodes.name: Transient_Proc
nodes.summary: Combined entry point for a shared thread: polls the trigger when armed and samples when recording.

nodes.name: Transient_ReadAt
nodes.summary: Reads back a captured sample by index, returning 0 beyond the recorded count.

nodes.name: Transient.h
nodes.summary: Interface of the one-shot transient data recorder: trigger and status enums, the mutable state and const context structs, allocation and init macros, inline status getters, and the control, trigger-poll, sample and readback API.
nodes.languageNotes: Const context struct (Transient_T) pointing at RAM state (Transient_State_T); the ALLOC macros build both from compound literals at file scope.

nodes.name: Transient_State_T
nodes.summary: Mutable recorder state: status, sample index, missed count, trigger tick, the runtime-tunable trigger type and threshold, and the previous trigger value for edge detection.

nodes.name: Transient_T
nodes.summary: Const recorder context binding the sampled variable and its size, the trigger variable and its size, the sample buffer and its length, and a pointer to the mutable state.

nodes.name: bits.h
nodes.summary: Bit utility header reduced to the bits_t typedef. The bit get/set, bit-mask and set-bit iteration helpers are all commented out.

nodes.name: bits_math.h
nodes.summary: Power-of-two alignment helpers on uintptr_t values: align down, align up, an alignment test and a mask test.

nodes.name: align_down
nodes.summary: Rounds a value down to a power-of-two alignment by masking with the negated alignment.

nodes.name: align_up
nodes.summary: Rounds a value up to a power-of-two alignment using two's-complement negation.

nodes.name: is_aligned
nodes.summary: Tests whether a value is a multiple of a power-of-two alignment.

nodes.name: is_masked
nodes.summary: Tests whether none of the bits selected by a mask are set in a value.

nodes.name: pwm_sample_sequences.txt
nodes.summary: Captured console tables from the PWM sample-sequence simulation: nominal ISR step durations, per-sequence sample-to-load timing, sweeps over the speed factor k and the loop order, arm margins for alternating sets, and a comparison of the triggered forms by load point.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Index of the motor simulation folder (SVPWM, current-sample sequences, sensorless geometry, PWM sample timing, atan2) and its conventions: script and PNG naming, the model / analysis / plot script split, board-agnostic content, output encoding, citing scripts from docs, and the Python environment.

nodes.name: sensorless_geometry.py
nodes.summary: Matplotlib script that draws the sensorless observer math as geometry, one PNG per component: the stator voltage polygon, Clarke and Park frames, the SMO error map, the low-pass filter, the phase detector and the angle PLL. Uses the float model in sensorless_model.py and prints the derived gains, poles and coefficients.
nodes.languageNotes: Runs headless with the Agg backend; small tuple-vector helpers (unit, add, scale, norm) and drawing primitives (arrow, label, frame, angle_arc) are shared by every figure function.

nodes.name: polygon_points
nodes.summary: Builds the vertices of the stator voltage polygon from the example R, X, E and current: R*i, then X*J*i, then the EMF up to v.

nodes.name: draw_polygon
nodes.summary: Draws the stator equation polygon on dq axes: the current, the R*i, X*J*i and EMF arrows and a right-angle marker.

nodes.name: fig_voltage_polygon
nodes.summary: Renders SensorlessVoltagePolygon.png: the stator equation as a closed polygon in the rotor frame, the EMF seen from the estimated frame, and the open polygon whose gap steps the model current.

nodes.name: fig_frames
nodes.summary: Renders SensorlessFrames.png: Clarke as three projections of one vector, Park as the same vector in a frame turned by the estimated angle, and the hold angle as the mean of an arc.

nodes.name: fig_smo
nodes.summary: Renders SensorlessSmo.png: the saturated switch and its balance point, the chatter and its low-pass mean as the equivalent control, and cobweb plots of the error map for three step gains. Returns the mean z and mean sigma of the chattering run.

nodes.name: fig_lpf
nodes.summary: Renders SensorlessLpf.png: the low-pass step response as a geometric series and its frequency response as a circle in the complex plane, marked at the cutoff.

nodes.name: fig_detector
nodes.summary: Renders SensorlessDetector.png: the rotor vector as the EMF turned a quarter turn back by the speed sign, the detector error as a parallelogram area with the magnitude floor and lock tolerance, and the detector S-curve.

nodes.name: simulate
nodes.summary: Runs the AnglePll model against a rotating reference angle and returns the angle error and the frequency slip per control cycle, with optional initial offsets and a speed step.

nodes.name: fig_pll
nodes.summary: Renders SensorlessPll.png: the loop as a ball on a washboard potential, its phase portrait at the default gains, and the response to a 20 Hz speed step.

nodes.name: print_numbers
nodes.summary: Prints the PLL's continuous-time gains, natural frequency and damping at 10 and 20 kHz, the SMO poles and fixed point, and the low-pass coefficients.

nodes.name: sensorless_model.py
nodes.summary: Float model of the sensorless math, mirroring the library's C functions for the stator current step, the sliding-mode observer, the low-pass filter, the rotor vector, the phase detector and the angle PLL. Per-unit quantities, radians, one control cycle per step.

nodes.name: stator_i_next
nodes.summary: One control-cycle step of the stator current model: i + G*(v - R*i - e), with G = 1/L.

nodes.name: J
nodes.summary: Quarter-turn rotation of a 2-vector: (d, q) becomes (-q, d).

nodes.name: smo_sat
nodes.summary: Saturation function of the sliding-mode observer: x / thr clamped to +/-1.

nodes.name: smo_sigma
nodes.summary: Sliding error: the estimated current minus the measured current.

nodes.name: smo_z
nodes.summary: Switching output of the observer: K_smo times the saturated sliding error.

nodes.name: lpf_step
nodes.summary: One step of a first-order low-pass filter: y + k*(x - y).

nodes.name: smo_error_map
nodes.summary: Maps the current estimation error across one step when model and plant share the same winding: (1 - G*R)*sigma - G*z(sigma) + G*e.

nodes.name: smo_pole
nodes.summary: Discrete pole of the error map inside the boundary layer: 1 - G*(R + K/thr).

nodes.name: smo_fixed_point
nodes.summary: Steady-state sliding error inside the boundary layer: e / (R + K/thr).

nodes.name: lpf_coef
nodes.summary: Low-pass coefficient for a cutoff frequency at a given control frequency, as in the EMF observer's default config.

nodes.name: foc_rotor_of_emf
nodes.summary: Turns the EMF vector a quarter turn back by the speed sign to get the vector along the rotor flux.

nodes.name: angle_pll_error
nodes.summary: Phase detector: the cross product of the input vector with the estimated-angle unit vector, |x|*sin(est - actual).

nodes.name: angle_pll_normalize
nodes.summary: Normalizes the detector error by the vector magnitude, returning 0 at or below the magnitude floor.

nodes.name: pll_gains
nodes.summary: Converts the angle PLL's default Q15 Kp and Ki into radians per control cycle for a given control frequency.

nodes.name: pll_continuous
nodes.summary: Derives the PLL's continuous-time gains, natural frequency and damping ratio from the per-cycle gains.

nodes.name: AnglePll
nodes.summary: Float model of the angle-tracking PLL, stepped once per control cycle: predict() advances the angle estimate by the speed estimate, and correct() runs the PI on the detector error to update the speed estimate.

nodes.name: sensorless_sequence.py
nodes.summary: Timeline simulation of the sensorless observer on the built current-loop sequence (KE06, 20 kHz PWM, 100 us control cycle). It extends the ISample scheduler with the observer prediction and three placements of its correction (A after the state machine, B between the take and the PI, and the removed thread form), then draws what each step reads and writes, the arm margins and the modeled-versus-applied voltage angle to SensorlessSequenceA.png and SensorlessSequenceB.png.
nodes.languageNotes: Reaches the ISample model through a sys.path insert, so those imports are invisible to static import resolution; SensorlessSim overrides the base pwm_isr generator to splice extra timed segments into the trace.

nodes.name: sensorless_sequence_fixed.py
nodes.summary: Variant of the sensorless timeline with two fixes that are not built: the correction moved after the arm into the PWM ISR between control cycles, and the hold angle turned by the sample-to-load delay. Reuses the simulator and plot of sensorless_sequence.py to write SensorlessSequenceFixed.png and print the checks.

nodes.name: MidClampBlend.md
nodes.summary: Note comparing the SVPWM duty ceiling with a zero-sequence blend scheduled on the voltage magnitude (not applied): how each placement splits the null time, where narrow pulses and clamped phases fall around the turn, why the motor sees none of it, and which simulation scripts and figures back each statement.

nodes.name: SVPWM_SectorID.py
nodes.summary: Models the sector form of midclamp SVPWM (line-to-line duties X, Y, Z and the sign-tree sector lookup of svpwm_midclamp_sector), checks it against the max/min form of svpwm_math.h, and plots both to SVPWM_SectorID.png.
nodes.languageNotes: Vectorised with numpy: np.select and np.isin replace the per-sample sector switch of the C implementation.

nodes.name: Saddle384.py
nodes.summary: Exploratory script that plots a hard-coded 384-entry saddle-shaped PWM lookup table (the space-vector duty waveform with its zero-clamped third) rescaled to percent duty. It defines no functions.

nodes.name: low_side_hold.py
nodes.summary: Track-and-hold model of a low-side R_DS(on) phase current sense under midclamp SVPWM: each PWM period a phase hold settles toward its true current only within its low-side window. Compares the current-vector error and its dq-frame harmonics when 3 phases or 2 of 3 are read, at Vbus/2 and Vbus/sqrt3, and writes LowSideHold.png.

nodes.name: low_side_window.py
nodes.summary: Computes the low-side conduction window per PWM period through the firmware integer output path (inverse Park, inverse Clarke, Vbus normalization, midclamp) in fract16 arithmetic. Compares the shortest window when 3 phases or 2 of 3 are read, checks the third phase solved from the current sum through Clarke, and writes LowSideWindow.png.

nodes.name: SensorlessSim
nodes.summary: Sim subclass with the observer selected: charges the prediction at CAPTURE_ANGLE in place of the Hall capture and splices the correction segments into the PWM ISR trace according to the form A, B or thread.

nodes.name: SensorlessSim.correction
nodes.summary: Generator yielding the correction segments: the thread form by instruction count per stage, or the on-take stages (v Park, SMO, detector, PLL) plus the hold for form A.

nodes.name: SensorlessSim.pwm_isr
nodes.summary: Wraps the base PWM ISR generator to insert the correction between the take and the PI (B), after the state machine (A) or after the PWM thread (thread), and the optional 1 ms speed poll segment.

nodes.name: seg_times
nodes.summary: Returns the start and end time of a labelled segment in one lane of the simulation trace for a given tick, or NaN when it did not run.

nodes.name: cycle_times
nodes.summary: Collects the instants of one control cycle from the trace: its sample, capture, prediction, take, write, load point and the correction stages.

nodes.name: arm_margin
nodes.summary: Time by which the between ISR finishes arming ahead of the trigger it arms for; a negative value means the set misses and waits a control cycle.

nodes.name: margin_text
nodes.summary: Formats an arm margin as "N us ahead" or "misses by N us" for the figure notes.

nodes.name: thread_spec
nodes.summary: Lane and step specification for the thread form: the value lanes, the labels of each cycle's values and which lanes every step reads and writes.

nodes.name: on_take_spec
nodes.summary: Returns the lane and step specification builder for forms A and B, where the FOC take is a lane of its own; A adds the held command lane, B reads v(k-1) where the loop left it.

nodes.name: cycles
nodes.summary: Cycle times for the control cycles k-2 to k+1 of a simulation run.

nodes.name: period_angles
nodes.summary: Mean frame angle of the applied and of the modeled voltage over the period a current sample closes, given how far the observer hold angle is turned back.

nodes.name: plot_timeline
nodes.summary: Draws the four-panel figure (PWM counter, ISR lanes, value lanes with read and write arrows, applied versus modeled voltage angle), saves it and prints the checks.

nodes.name: main_on_take
nodes.summary: Runs forms A and B against the base and the thread timelines, derives arm margins, load timing and the modeled-to-applied angle gap, and plots SensorlessSequenceA.png and SensorlessSequenceB.png with their notes.

nodes.name: next_cycle
nodes.summary: For the cycle after the correction: how late its PWM ISR starts, when it writes relative to its top, and the load point that results.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Simulates the correction placed after the arm, computes arm margins and next-cycle delays at duration factors 1 and 1.2, with and without the speed tick, evaluates the hold angle turned by the load delay, and plots SensorlessSequenceFixed.png.

nodes.name: line_to_line
nodes.summary: Returns the three basic vector magnitudes X, Y, Z from alpha and beta in duty scaling, which are also the line-to-line duties B-C, A-C and B-A.

nodes.name: sector
nodes.summary: Sign tree that maps X, Y, Z to the SVPWM sector number 1 to 6.

nodes.name: svpwm_midclamp_sector
nodes.summary: Sector form of midclamp: opposite sectors share one case, the mid phase takes the zero-sequence offset and the other two follow by the line-to-line duties; the result is clipped to 0..1.

nodes.name: svpwm_midclamp
nodes.summary: Max/min form of midclamp as in svpwm_math.h: subtracts the mean of the highest and lowest phase voltage and centers the duties on 1/2.

nodes.name: duties
nodes.summary: Midclamp duties of a balanced three-phase voltage set of radius r per Vbus at angle theta.

nodes.name: clarke
nodes.summary: Amplitude-invariant Clarke transform of three phase quantities to alpha and beta.

nodes.name: simulate
nodes.summary: Steps the three holds through whole electrical cycles after settling, each moving toward its true current by the fraction its low-side window allows, optionally solving the highest-duty phase from the other two with handoff hysteresis, and returns the error angle, magnitude and dq components.

nodes.name: harmonics

nodes.name: duties
nodes.summary: Reproduces the firmware output path in fract16 for a dq command at theta: inverse Park, inverse Clarke, normalization by Vbus and midclamp, returning the three duties.

nodes.name: window_us

nodes.name: foc_clarke

nodes.name: low_side_zero_sequence.py
nodes.summary: Compares zero-sequence placements for a low-side current sense: midclamp, the general clamp k, the bottom clamp and the duty ceiling. For each placement, circle radius and read mode it reports the shortest low-side window through the integer output path, the track-and-hold current-vector error and the PWM ripple current RMS, and writes LowSideZeroSequence.png.

nodes.name: low_side_zero_sequence_blend.py

Per placement and radius it reports duty continuity, the shortest low-side window, the angle with narrow pulses or a clamped phase, ripple RMS and the track-and-hold error, and writes LowSideZeroSequenceBlend.png.

nodes.name: svpwm_clamp_k.py
nodes.summary: Generates SVPWM_Clamp_K.svg, a script-free SMIL animation of the general clamp k: the three duties over one turn, the PWM period at the line-to-line peak and the counter-compare view, showing that k moves the null time between O000 and O111 while the line-to-line voltages stay fixed.
nodes.languageNotes: Builds the SVG as strings with SMIL <animate> elements keyed at the k holds; duty is linear in k, so keyframe interpolation is exact and no JavaScript is needed in the image.

nodes.name: svpwm_midclamp.py
nodes.summary: Simulates midclamp SVPWM over one electrical cycle at the linear limit and plots the three duties, the normalized phase voltages and the injected zero-sequence voltage to SVPWM_Midclamp.png.

nodes.name: atan2.py
nodes.summary: Prototype of a fixed-point atan2 approximation: a cubic in the ratio r = (x - |y|)/(x + |y|) with a quadrant offset, evaluated over one revolution and plotted against sine and cosine in fract16 scale.
nodes.languageNotes: Follows the same structure as fract16_atan2 in Math/Fixed/fract16.c, with coefficients in a radian fixed-point scale rather than angle16.

nodes.name: pwm_sample_timing.py
nodes.summary: Models one center-aligned PWM period on a KE0x FTM: the counter, phase PWM, conducting switch, low-side sample window and ripple current, and what each ADC conversion reads when started at the counter top (today) or at the bottom init trigger (the option). Writes PwmSampleTiming.png.
