nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Describes MotCan, which exposes every MotVarId as a CANopen manufacturer-specific object behind the standard SDO server. Part 1 covers the generic CiA 301 SDO and object-dictionary contract (COB-IDs, the expedited frame, command byte, abort codes); Part 2 covers the MotVarId to index/subindex mapping, admission, the access model and a worked example, followed by a code map of the implementing headers.

nodes.name: MotPacket_Frame.md
nodes.summary: Reference sheet for the MotPacket serial codec: its two wire shapes (4-byte control frame and 8-byte-header data frame), what each checksum covers, how the wire Length relates to the engine payload length, which ids are fixed or variable length, the receive parser bounds and the open issues.

nodes.name: VarIdMap.md
nodes.summary: Address-space map of the 16-bit MotVarId: one row per (Prefix, Type) giving the Get and Set handler it reaches, the write admission policy, the instance range and whether the host application's Dart enum matches, together with the dispatch flow and a list of gaps found in the code.

nodes.name: CurrentSampling.md
nodes.summary: Sheet on phase current sampling: where the sample sits in the PWM period for a low-side sensor, how the conversion starts (marks before the duty write, software start or hardware trigger) and where the current loop takes the sample, with the build options that move it.

nodes.name: Motor_Instance.h
nodes.summary: Placeholder header that holds only a commented-out sketch of a per-instance Motor_Entity_T wrapper (motor, heat monitor, ADC conversion, adapter buffer) for extensions the core motor logic does not need.

nodes.name: PwmConvention.md
nodes.summary: Defines the PWM convention the motor layer writes duties in: center-aligned high-true duty, the phase current sign, the counter top and bottom events and the duty load points. Walks through one period using the simulated timing figure.

nodes.name: RotorSensorInterface.md
nodes.summary: Describes the RotorSensor_T rotor angle sensor interface: its vtable, shared state and registry, the Hall, Encoder, SinCos and Sensorless implementations, what each does in every operation, the order the motor calls them in, and the sensor-owned state machine sub-states.

nodes.name: ILimitsRouting.md
nodes.summary: Mermaid flowchart of how current limits reach a motor's active clamp: live sources (MOSFET heat, optional digital input, user, protocol, VBus voltage) and stored config pass through frame conversions and merge points into Motor_ResolveILimits, with the threads and call sites that invoke each step. Also traces the parallel speed-derate path and names the compile-time options that select which thread resolves ISupplyLimits.

nodes.name: MotorController_StateMachine.md
nodes.summary: Reference sheet for the controller-level state machine: the root states (INIT, STANDBY, MAIN, MOTOR_TUNING, LOCK, FAULT) with their entries, inputs, lock ids, fault flags and per-state write admission, plus the thread each part runs on. Also covers the Traction app sub-states (NEUTRAL, DRIVE) mounted under MAIN and the startup, drive and fault sequences.

nodes.name: MotorController_Traction.md
nodes.summary: Cross-layer view of the controller state tree with the Traction leaves: a table mapping every motor-facing call made by the Traction and controller states to the motor input it becomes and how each motor state responds. Sequence diagrams cover throttle press, brake to hold, direction change at speed, E_STOP under the zero modes and fault handling, followed by the source list and open issues.

nodes.name: _CAN.h
nodes.summary: Draft header holding an ISO 11898 CAN / CAN FD frame field reference in comments, with commented-out standard and extended wire-ID bitfield structs and a frame-type enum. It only includes stdint.h and declares no active types or functions.

nodes.name: Notes.md
nodes.summary: Design notes for the Peripheral layer: HAL modules are single-register-operation inline functions bound by include path instead of vtables, with the rationale (call cost on Cortex-M0+, compile-time interface check) and the boundaries where tables are used instead. Covers platform-prefixed functions, the default and override mechanisms, host test doubles selected through an alternate HAL directory, and the Pin / FastPin exception.

nodes.name: WritePath.md
nodes.summary: Traces the blocking flash write path from MotNvm_SaveConfigAll_Blocking through Flash.c and NvMemory.c to the flash controller command: the call chain, which functions must execute from RAM, the interrupt-off span of each operation, the op-control table and the admission checks (partition, alignment, size, buffer, busy). Closes with open issues such as the unverified save and the remainder write reaching past the admitted range.

nodes.name: _md
nodes.summary: Scratch Mermaid fragment sketching the NvMemory layering: the NvMemory engine owns all operation state (address, size, buffer), calls through the OpControl_T / HalBase_T vtable seam, and reaches HAL_Flash_* functions that only write registers.

nodes.name: Reboot.h
nodes.summary: Include-guarded placeholder header whose CMSIS-based Reboot() (disable IRQs, clear the NVIC enable and pending bits, NVIC_SystemReset) is entirely commented out, so it declares nothing. The same reset sequence lives in the platform HAL_Reboot.

nodes.name: Encoder_Reference.md
nodes.summary: Flow reference for how an incremental encoder acquires an absolute reference: the align and index (Z) datums, the three angle frames (d-axis, index, user), the monotonic NONE / ALIGNED / HOMED reference state lattice, and one align-then-sweep acquisition procedure with three terminal actions (calibrate, run, home). Details the two-store index ISR, the armed capture sentinel and the promotion done by the polling thread.

nodes.name: Monitor_Derate.h
nodes.summary: Header containing only a commented-out Monitor_WarningDerateScale helper that would map an input linearly from the warning setpoint (full scale) down to the fault setpoint (zero). It declares nothing; the heat monitor's limit scale is the derate in use.

nodes.name: Monitor_Group.h
nodes.summary: Commented-out design sketches for grouping monitors: Monitor_Context_T and MonitorGroup_T const-context structs and several poll strategies (poll each and find the greatest input, track the worst status, round-robin). Nothing in the file is compiled.

nodes.name: _Monitor_Status.h
nodes.summary: Commented-out alternative Monitor_Status_T enum with seven ISA-18.2 style severity levels (normal, advisory, caution, warning, alarm, critical, fault). Kept as a reference only; the active three-level status is defined in Monitor.h.

nodes.name: MonitorStatus.md
nodes.summary: Sheet for the single-direction Monitor_T: how each poll evaluates NORMAL, WARNING or FAULT from the input, the warning hysteresis band and fault limit laid out on one axis for the HIGH and LOW directions, and how config fields map to their runtime copies. Also explains the heat monitor's linear derate between the warning and fault setpoints, the RangeMonitor composition, and open issues.

nodes.name: PulseEncoder.h
nodes.summary: Fully commented-out draft of a PulseEncoder composite pairing a PulseTimer (edge timing) with an AngleCounter (count and angle math) as one pulse-driven angle and speed engine for Hall, soft-decoded encoder, BEMF zero-cross and tachometer inputs. It sketches edge-ISR capture, sample-rate frequency capture and init helpers but declares nothing.
nodes.languageNotes: The draft follows the library's const-context pattern: a const outer struct (PulseEncoder_T) holds configuration and a pointer to the bundled mutable state (PulseEncoder_State_T).

layers.name: Fixed-Point Math
layers.description: Dependency-free numerics for runtime fixed-point control: fract16 and angle16 formats, angle and speed counters with a PLL, PID, ramps, linear maps, moving average, accumulator, hysteresis and threshold, plus the Math/HAL fixed-or-float selector. It imports nothing outside Math, as ARCHITECTURE.md states.

layers.name: Peripheral & System
layers.description: The hardware access layer: Peripheral drivers (ADC, PWM, CAN, UART, SPI, Pin, ClockTimer, NvMemory Flash/EEPROM, the Xcvr transport interface) bound at compile time to the chip HAL in Peripheral/HAL/Platform/KE0x, merged here with the six-file System module (Critical, SysTime, Reboot, BootRef) that wraps the Cortex-M core. One include runs upward: UART.h uses Framework/Ring.

layers.name: Framework
layers.description: Reusable engines and containers: the hierarchical StateMachine, the Protocol/Socket packet engine with Datagram, data-mode and flash-loader extensions, Ring, Timer, LimitArray, Transient, and the Framework/Type helpers (Array, Bits, Field, Word, accessor). The README calls it hardware-independent and ARCHITECTURE.md says it has no peripheral access, but Protocol.h includes Peripheral/Xcvr and Protocol_FlashLoader.h calls Peripheral/NvMemory Flash; the StateMachine lock and Ring also depend on System/Critical.

layers.name: Transducer
layers.description: Sensor and actuator algorithms that turn peripheral signals into measurements and user commands: quadrature Encoder, Pulse timers, voltage, heat and range Monitors with thermistor and divider conversion, debounced UserIn analog and digital inputs, and the Blinky pin pattern. It sits on Peripheral as the README says, and on Math; Encoder and PulseTimer also bind directly to chip HAL headers, and Blinky uses Framework/Timer.

layers.name: Motor FOC Math & Models
layers.description: Pure field-oriented control math with no hardware access (Motor/Motor/Math and Model): Clarke/Park transforms, SVPWM zero-sequence placement and modulation limits, the FOC_T dq state with its PI pair, motor electrical per-unit math, stator and sensorless observer equations, and the Stator, EmfObserver, Motor_Limits and Motor_Types models, with their limit and modulation notes.

layers.name: Motor Phase & Bus I/O
layers.description: The motor stack's electrical boundary, where Motor/Motor meets Peripheral PWM/ADC/Pin and Transducer/Monitor: Phase_VOut, Phase_Svpwm and Phase_Polar write duties and gate states, Phase_Input, Phase_ADC and Motor_ADC capture per-unit phase voltage and current, and VBus tracks the DC bus with its monitor, config and derating.

layers.name: Motor Control Core
layers.description: The per-motor aggregate and control law: Motor_T config, context and handle (Motor.h/.c), the Motor_FOC per-PWM-cycle current and voltage pipelines, the Motor_Config field interface, the Motor_Electrical model and Motor_Clock loop rates, with the control-cycle and limit-chain notes and the stack's Version.h. Every higher Motor layer includes Motor.h, while Motor.h itself includes the RotorSensor interface from the sensor layer.

layers.name: Motor State Machine & Interface
layers.description: Per-motor behaviour and its outward surface: the hierarchical Motor_StateMachine with its Calibration, OpenLoop and Intervention sub-states, plus the files that feed and run it: Motor_User commands and telemetry, the Motor_Var var-id interface, Motor_Thread ISR and loop entry points, the Motor_Include umbrella and the Extension helpers. Grouped by dependency direction: these call into the state machine, which drives Motor.c and Motor_FOC.c in the core, and the protocol and controller layers enter the motor through this layer.

layers.name: Motor Rotor Sensors
layers.description: Rotor angle and speed feedback behind the RotorSensor vtable and per-motor sensor table, with Hall, Encoder, SinCos and Sensorless implementations built on Transducer/Encoder and Pulse, and the sensorless design notes. The dependency with the layers below is two-way: Motor.h includes the RotorSensor interface, while each Motor_<Sensor> integration file includes Motor.h and Motor_StateMachine.h to supply calibration and start-up sub-states.

layers.name: Motor Protocol
layers.description: Wire engines and variable maps for host and GUI communication (Motor/MotProtocol): the MotPacket serial codec and flash-loader handlers on Framework/Protocol, CANopen SDO/PDO, the CiA 402 drive profile, the MotCan manufacturer service, and the MotVarId id space with its Motor_MotVar dispatch. ARCHITECTURE.md says the engines know nothing of the controller, yet at folder level the dependency is two-way: MotorController_Cia402 and MotorController_MotCan here include controller headers, and the controller's Var files include MotVarId.

layers.name: Motor Controller
layers.description: Application layer coordinating all motors (Motor/MotorController): the controller state machine, MotorController_T wiring of the motor table, ADC, UART, CAN and protocol sockets, var-id routing and MotProtocol request handlers, analog user inputs (throttle, brake, shifter, option pins), the Traction app mode, buzzer, limits and MotNvm persistence. Also holds the Motor stack-root notes (DependencyGraph, StateMachineOverview, ThreadOwnership, todo), which span the whole stack.

layers.name: Simulation Tooling
layers.description: Python models, analysis and plot scripts under Motor/Docs/Simulation with their notes and captured output: SVPWM zero-sequence, ceiling and blend studies, current-sample sequencing against PWM timing, sensorless observer geometry and timelines, and a fixed-point atan2 prototype. Self-contained tooling outside the firmware build: firmware notes cite it, and no C file depends on it.

layers.name: Project Documentation & Meta
layers.description: Project-wide guidance rather than module notes: README, ARCHITECTURE and CLAUDE at the root, the Docs tree of Principles, Conventions, Patterns, Decisions and Findings with its indexes, and the repository meta files (.clang-format, .gitattributes, the dormant library.json).

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: FireSourcery Library is an embedded C library with a field-oriented motor control stack for bare-metal Cortex-M0+ and Cortex-M4 targets: no RTOS, no heap after init, and fixed-point math at runtime. README.md introduces the layer layout (Motor, Peripheral, System, Transducer, Math, Framework), and ARCHITECTURE.md adds the design patterns, the layer and motor-stack dependency diagrams, and the integration steps with the thread entry-point table. The library has no main(); a separate board project calls it from a 20 kHz PWM interrupt and a 1 ms main loop, so this tour climbs the layers bottom-up toward the entry points that project uses.

tour.title: Fixed-Point Math Foundations
tour.description: Everything above this layer computes in fixed point, so it comes first. fract16.h defines the Q1.15 types (fract16_t, accum32_t) with inline multiply, divide and saturation and is one of the most depended-on headers in the library, while FixedPoint.md explains the three quantity families (per-unit, time in ticks of a named clock, and angle as a turn / 2^16) and the rules for combining them. On top sit small stateful objects that the motor stack composes: Angle_T integrates an angle that wraps by integer overflow, PID_T is the PI controller state with its gains and output limits, and Ramp_T slews a setpoint toward a stored target. The Math layer imports nothing outside itself, which keeps it usable on its own.
tour.languageLesson: Q1.15 fixed point: a fract16_t stores a value in [-1, 1) as an int16_t scaled by 2^15. Multiplying two fractions gives a 32-bit product that is shifted right by 15 to return to Q1.15, and a wider accumulator type such as accum32_t holds intermediate results that may exceed 1.0 until they are saturated back to 16 bits. An angle uses the same trick differently: with 65536 counts per turn, wrap-around is ordinary integer overflow.

tour.title: Hierarchical State Machine Engine
tour.description: The Framework layer holds reusable engines, and the hierarchical state machine is the one the motor stack relies on most. Each state is a const State_T: ENTRY, EXIT and LOOP actions, an input transition table and a parent link, so the states form a tree in ROM with one active-leaf pointer in RAM per machine instance. StateMachine.h is the public handle and guarded input API; behind it, _StateMachine_Tree.c walks the tree, running exit and entry actions between the active leaf and a target state, and _StateMachine_Lock.h selects at compile time how asynchronous inputs are synchronized with the periodic process step. Architecture.md explains the handlers, the tree walk, one process cycle and the threading, and is worth reading before the motor and controller machines in steps 10 and 12.
tour.languageLesson: Vtables in C: State_T is a const struct of function pointers plus data (handlers, a transition table, a parent pointer). Because every state is a const object it is placed in flash, and the machine keeps only a pointer to the active one in RAM, so a transition is a pointer assignment wrapped in the exit and entry calls. A leading underscore on a header (_StateMachine.h, _State.h) marks the private or protected part of a module.

tour.title: Protocol Engine and Sockets
tour.description: The second Framework engine is a non-blocking packet protocol, which the wire-protocol step near the end of the tour builds on. Packet.h defines the frame vocabulary and the Packet_Codec_T table of framing callbacks, Protocol_Request.h looks up the handler for each packet id in a const request table, and Protocol.h composes parsing, ack and retransmission handling and dispatch into one pass over an Xcvr transport. Socket.h bundles one engine with its transport selection and NVM-backed port configuration into the instance an application polls. The README diagrams the receive pipeline and traces the four request shapes.
tour.languageLesson: Callback tables with an opaque context: the engine holds a void pointer to the application context and const tables of function pointers (a codec and a request table), and hands the context back on every call. The engine therefore never includes application headers, and a new wire format is added by supplying tables rather than by editing the engine.

tour.title: Peripheral Drivers and HAL
tour.description: The Peripheral layer gives upper layers one interface per peripheral (ADC, PWM, Pin, UART, CAN, NvMemory and others) and keeps register access behind a chip HAL. Peripheral/Notes.md explains the central choice: HAL modules are single-register-operation inline functions bound by include path instead of vtables, which avoids call cost on Cortex-M0+ and checks the interface at compile time. HAL_Peripheral.h defines the HAL_PERIPHERAL_PATH() macro that resolves each HAL header to a chip directory such as Platform/KE0x, where HAL_PWM.h programs the FlexTimer for center-aligned PWM. PWM.h and ADC.h are the portable drivers on top, and they are the two that the motor's phase output and current sensing use in step 8.
tour.languageLesson: Compile-time polymorphism: instead of a function-pointer table, each chip directory provides a header of the same name with the same inline functions, and a macro-built #include path picks one at build time. The register write is inlined at the call site, so the abstraction costs nothing at run time and a missing function is a compile error rather than a null pointer. The same mechanism lets a host build point at an alternate HAL directory of test doubles.

tour.title: Transducers: Sensors and Inputs
tour.description: Transducers turn peripheral signals into measurements and user commands, sitting on the Peripheral and Math layers. Encoder.h is the incremental encoder core, with hardware-decoder or software-emulated capture, and PulseTimer.h times square-wave edges on the HAL clock timer; both return in step 11 as parts of the rotor sensors. Monitor.h evaluates an input as NORMAL, WARNING or FAULT against a fault limit and a warning hysteresis band, as MonitorStatus.md lays out on one axis, and is the base for the voltage and heat monitors. UserAIn.h handles a potentiometer-style throttle or brake input, the kind of command source the controller reads in step 12.

tour.title: FOC Math and Models
tour.description: The motor stack begins with math that has no hardware access. foc_math.h holds the Clarke and Park transforms, decoupling feedforward and voltage-circle limiting as pure fixed-point functions, and svpwm_math.h holds the zero-sequence placements that turn phase voltages into duties. FOC.h wraps them in FOC_T, the object that carries the dq, alpha-beta and abc vectors and the Id/Iq PI pair built from the PID of step 2. ModulationLimit.md explains how the low-side current-sense window sets the modulation limit, and EmfObserver.h is the stator-model observer that the sensorless sensor uses in step 11.
tour.languageLesson: Pure functions under stateful objects: lower-case headers such as foc_math.h and svpwm_math.h hold stateless inline functions that take and return values, while the capitalised FOC.h defines a _T struct and the functions that operate on it. The same pairing appears in the Math layer (linear_math.h under Linear.h). Keeping the equations pure lets them be checked off-target and mirrored by the Python models in step 14.

tour.title: Phase Output and Current Sensing
tour.description: This is the electrical boundary, where the FOC math meets the PWM and ADC drivers of step 5. Phase_VOut_T is the inverter actuator (a PWM module, three PWM channels and three gate pins), and Phase_Svpwm.h bridges FOC phase voltages to duties by normalizing with the inverse bus voltage and applying the build-selected zero-sequence placement. On the input side, Motor_ADC.h converts phase voltage and current ADC counts into per-unit values and marks the next conversions. PwmConvention.md fixes the duty polarity and phase current sign, and CurrentSampling.md shows where the low-side current sample sits in the PWM period and how the conversion is started.

tour.title: The Motor Object
tour.description: Motor.h is the hub of the stack: it defines the storable Motor_Config_T, the runtime Motor_Context_T and the const Motor_T handle that gathers the pieces from the earlier steps, including the phase output, FOC state, PIDs, ramps and rotor sensor. Motor.c initialises a motor from its NVM config, and Motor_FOC.c holds the per-PWM-cycle current-mode and voltage-mode pipelines that end in the SVPWM duty write. Motor_Thread.h is the entry surface a board project places in its ISRs and loops: the PWM-rate control thread captures the sensor, steps the state machine and polls speed. ControlCycleDataFlow.md follows one cycle from ADC counts to the PWM compare registers, naming the field, fixed-point unit and owning thread at each step.
tour.languageLesson: Object-oriented C: the object is split by where it is stored. Motor_Config_T is the persisted part, Motor_Context_T is the RAM state, and const Motor_T is a flash-resident handle that points to both and carries the hardware bindings. Functions take a pointer to the handle, or to the narrowest part they read or write, in place of an implicit this.

tour.title: Motor State Machine
tour.description: Each motor's behaviour is an instance of the state machine engine from step 3. Motor_StateMachine.c defines the root states INIT, DEACTIVATED, PASSIVE, RUN, INTERVENTION, OPEN_LOOP, CALIBRATION and FAULT, whose handlers drive the Motor_FOC pipelines of step 9 and whose input tables handle fault, phase output, feedback mode and direction requests. The machine is processed on the PWM thread while inputs arrive from the main thread, which is why the commands declared in Motor_User.h are routed through it instead of writing motor state directly. Motor_StateMachine.md is the module sheet for states, inputs and fault flags, and Motor_StateTree.md maps every root, leaf and hand-off, including the open-loop, intervention and calibration sub-states.

tour.title: Rotor Sensors and Sensorless
tour.description: FOC needs the rotor's electrical angle and speed every cycle, and RotorSensor.h supplies them through one interface: a const vtable (capture angle, capture speed, feedback availability, zeroing) over a shared state holding electrical angle, per-cycle delta and per-unit speed. Hall_Sensor.h implements it by composing the Hall decoder with the PulseTimer of step 6 and an angle counter, snapping to the sector boundary on each edge and interpolating within the sector at 20 kHz. Sensorless_Sensor.c implements the same vtable with the EmfObserver of step 7, predicting the PLL angle every control tick and correcting it from the sampled currents and held voltage. RotorSensorInterface.md compares the Hall, Encoder, SinCos and Sensorless implementations operation by operation, and Sensorless.md covers the observer and its start-up chain.
tour.languageLesson: Inheritance by composition: a concrete sensor struct embeds the RotorSensor base next to its own data, and a const vtable instance such as HALL_VTABLE or ENCODER_VTABLE supplies its operations; inline wrappers in RotorSensor.h dispatch through the table. A no-op vtable fills the slot for unselected sensors, so callers never null-check a function pointer.

tour.title: Multi-Motor Controller
tour.description: MotorController_T is the application-level object a board project instantiates: one const allocation wiring the motor table, the ADC, UART and CAN peripherals, user inputs, voltage and heat monitors, protocol sockets, NVM and its own state machine. MotorController_Thread.h provides the thread bodies to map onto execution contexts: the main loop (1 ms state machine output, protocol sockets, inputs), a 1 ms timer thread, and the PWM thread that marks ADC channels and runs the per-motor control of step 9. The controller's hierarchical machine (Init, Standby, Main, MotorTuning, Lock, Fault) coordinates all motors, and an application mode such as Traction mounts its sub-states under Main. Because several execution contexts share state, ThreadOwnership.md lists every field that one context writes and another reads.

tour.title: Wire Protocol and Variable IDs
tour.description: Host tools and the GUI reach the controller through the protocol engine of step 4. MotPacket.h defines the serial wire format (packet ids, sync and data headers, payload structs), and MotorController_MotProtocol.c supplies the request table binding each packet id to a handler for ping, version, variable read and write, and memory access. Variables are addressed by MotVarId_T, a 16-bit identifier (base, type, prefix, instance) shared by all transports; VarIdMap.md maps each prefix and type to its Get and Set handler and write admission policy. The MotCan README shows the same ids exposed over CAN as CANopen manufacturer-specific objects behind a standard SDO server.
tour.languageLesson: Typed wire data: MotVarId_T packs four fields into 16 bits and checks the field widths at compile time, and a packet is a union of packed payload structs over one buffer. Handlers read named fields instead of indexing bytes, and a field-width mistake in the id fails the build instead of surfacing on the wire.

tour.title: Simulation Tooling
tour.description: Design choices in the firmware are backed by Python models kept under Motor/Docs/Simulation, outside the firmware build. svpwm_ceiling.py models the svpwm_midclamp_ceiling placement from svpwm_math.h and is the base module the other SVPWM studies import, isample_model.py and pwm_sample_timing.py model the current-sample sequence against PWM and ADC timing on a KE0x-class MCU, and sensorless_model.py is a float mirror of the observer's C functions. The README indexes the folder and its split into model, analysis and plot scripts. Read these alongside the notes of steps 7, 8 and 11, which use their figures.

tour.title: Conventions, Patterns and Decisions
tour.description: The Docs tree records why the code looks the way it does, and Docs/README.md indexes it: Principles, Conventions, Patterns, Decisions and Findings, plus the rule that module notes live beside their source. Naming.md explains the underscore-scoped names seen throughout the tour, Config_State_Ref.md the split between persisted config and runtime state, and Descriptor.md the const descriptor struct behind handles such as Motor_T. Decisions/README.md indexes the architecture decision records, the place to look before changing behaviour that crosses layers. Dot-prefixed folders hold design sketches and retired code outside the library proper; this graph leaves them out.
tour.languageLesson: The const descriptor as a template argument: a typedef const struct holds bindings, compile-time constants and pointers to the mutable parts, and is passed to inline functions. The compiler folds its fields at the inlined call site, so a generic primitive is specialised per instance without macros and without run-time cost.
